Exact contract rules, exceptional payouts, and collateral understood. Read the specific contract's own rules document, not a general description of "how this kind of market usually works." Identify whether an exceptional settlement, dispute process, or partial payout is possible, and in what collateral; Polymarket's documented dispute and 50/50 payout process, and its separate pUSD-versus-USDC collateral distinction, are concrete examples of detail a short title cannot convey. POLYMARKET_RESOLUTION POLYMARKET_COLLATERAL

Real point-in-time evidence independently reviewed after strategy search. Any forecasting claim behind a real trade needs evaluation on data genuinely available at decision time, with every trial and adjustment logged, in the sense of Chapter 19, not merely "backtested well once it looked good." Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado, and Zhu's backtest-overfitting framework is the relevant qualified reminder that repeated holdout inspection during research is itself a mechanism for producing an impressive but unreliable result. BAILEY2017

Current fees, rounding, executable depth, and maximum affordable loss checked. Re-verify the venue's actual, currently effective fee schedule immediately before trading, since documented fee tables and rounding rules are explicitly time-varying. KALSHI_ROUNDING POLYMARKET_FEES Confirm executable depth at the price you intend to pay, not a stale quote, and compute the maximum possible loss using the same cost-basis arithmetic as Section 30.3 before doing anything else.

Open inventory, reserved cash, and correlated loss reviewed. Account for existing positions' combined loss under a joint adverse scenario, not each in isolation; Chapter 22's bankroll discussion and this book's scenario_stress helper both exist because individually small positions can produce an unacceptable combined loss under correlated events.

A written manual decision, rejection conditions and outcome journal prepared. Before placing any order, write down why you believe the trade is justified, the conditions under which you would consider yourself wrong and exit, and a place to honestly record the eventual outcome. This is not a bureaucratic formality; it is the defense against rationalizing a bad decision, or forgetting how many similar decisions were actually made and how they turned out.

docs.title: 30.6 Why the evidence gate cannot be toggled into a live pass
docs.text:
Read prediction_market_lab.evidence.assess_evidence directly. It accepts six explicit boolean fields, point_in_time_verified, execution_history_verified, costs_verified, untouched_evaluation, dependence_and_search_accounted_for, and uncertainty_supports_positive_net_result, plus a synthetic flag and a nonempty provenance tuple, and it raises ValueError outright if any of these is not a genuine boolean. Suppose, hypothetically, a reader constructed an Evidence object with synthetic=False, real provenance strings, and every one of those six booleans set to True, representing a claim that every one of these six conditions had actually been satisfied by real, independently reviewed work. Even in that best possible case, assess_evidence does not return anything resembling a "cleared to trade live" status. It returns RESEARCH_REVIEW_REQUIRED, with the explicit accompanying reason "declarations require independent audit; no automatic live promotion".

There is no flag that converts a paper decision into a funded one. Complete declarations can request independent research review, not perform that review or authorize an order. synthetic_evidence() sets synthetic=True and point_in_time_verified=True for the fixture's explicitly constructed teaching clocks; its remaining five verification flags are false. This does not certify real historical availability: the separate synthetic flag itself blocks empirical live-edge inference. Every quickstart therefore returns REJECT_LIVE_EDGE_INFERENCE, describing its actual evidence rather than imposing an arbitrary penalty.

docs.title: 30.7 There is no paper-to-live unlock, and this chapter does not invent one
docs.text: Nothing in the book's educational companion stores an API key, signs a transaction, submits a funded order, or contains a hidden or documented switch that promotes a paper decision, however favorable, into a live one. This boundary applies to book\companion, not to separate trading-system code elsewhere in the repository. The market_data module, documented in data/README.md and the examples README, performs only optional, explicitly acknowledged (--acknowledge-terms) read-only public metadata and order-book snapshot requests against four allowlisted endpoints; it has no coupling to PaperBroker, no order-submission capability, and no credential handling, and it is neither a live broker nor a historical archive. No default example calls it, the companion ships no acquired venue payload, and its output is a separate, locally gitignored file a reader must explicitly request. A separately documented mock-funds demo and a documented live/historical data split at one venue are likewise not a claim of live-market execution fidelity or a complete historical order-book archive; treat any paper, demo, or historical-replay result as rehearsal, not proof. KALSHI_DEMO KALSHI_HISTORY A first real trade, if a reader independently decides to make one after completing every check in Section 30.5, happens entirely outside the educational companion, on a venue's own interface, under its own account, terms, and current operative rules. This book supplies the accounting discipline, the failure vocabulary, and the checklist; it does not, and by design cannot, supply the trade itself.

docs.title: 30.8 Troubleshooting
docs.text: If you find yourself editing evidence.py or the checklist script to force a different status, stop: that would not create real verified evidence, only relabel the exact same synthetic fixtures this chapter has already accounted for. If you are unsure whether a real check genuinely satisfies one of Section 30.5's six items, hold the corresponding flag at False rather than rounding it up; an explicit boolean should describe only what has actually been verified. If your written decision record from Section 30.5's sixth check feels uncomfortable to write honestly, that discomfort is informative and should not be resolved by skipping the exercise.

docs.title: Exercise 1: recomputing the canonical numbers from memory
docs.text:
Without looking back at Section 30.3, write down the cost, the two settlement outcomes, the modeled expected profit at \(\hat p = 0.55\), and the realized resale profit for the book's canonical ten-unit example, then check your answer.

Solution sketch. Cost is \(10\times(0.40+0.01)=4.10\); settlement outcomes are \(+5.90\) on YES and \(-4.10\) on NO; modeled expected profit at \(\hat p=0.55\) is \(10\times(0.55-0.41)=1.40\); realized resale profit at a bid of 0.46 with a further 0.01 exit fee is \(10\times(0.46-0.40-0.01-0.01)=0.40\).

docs.title: Exercise 2: a first-dollar target at a different price
docs.text:
Using the same USD 0.01 per-unit fee, find the smallest whole-unit quantity that produces at least USD 2.00 of profit if the position resolves YES, at an ask of 0.55 instead of 0.40.

Solution sketch. Per-unit cost is \(0.55+0.01=0.56\); per-unit profit if YES is \(1.00-0.56=0.44\). Solving \(Q\times0.44\geq2.00\) gives \(Q\geq4.545\ldots\), so the smallest whole quantity is \(Q=5\), costing \(5\times0.56=2.80\) and producing a planned if-YES profit of \(5\times0.44=2.20\), with a maximum loss of 2.80 if the position instead resolves NO.

docs.title: Exercise 3: why RESEARCH_REVIEW_REQUIRED is not a green light
docs.text:
A reader argues that since RESEARCH_REVIEW_REQUIRED is a materially different, less severe status than REJECT_LIVE_EDGE_INFERENCE, reaching it should be treated as sufficient grounds to place a live trade. Explain what is wrong with this argument.

Solution sketch. RESEARCH_REVIEW_REQUIRED means only that the declared evidence conditions, if honestly true, would justify independent human research review; its own accompanying reason states explicitly that it requires independent audit and grants no automatic live promotion. It is a description of what evidence would be worth someone's further scrutiny, not a verdict that the underlying claims have actually been audited, or that they are correct, or that the resulting trading decision is safe. Treating it as a green light substitutes a code path's internal label for the actual human review that label is asking for.

docs.title: Exercise 4: a maximum-loss check across two correlated positions
docs.text:
A reader already holds the canonical ten-unit position from Section 30.2, with a maximum loss of 4.10, and is considering the two-unit position from Section 30.4, with a maximum loss of 0.82, where both contracts' resolutions are known to be strongly positively correlated. State the appropriate combined maximum-loss figure to use when deciding whether this fits an affordable-loss limit, and explain why simply adding the two average losses would understate the relevant risk.

Solution sketch. Under strong positive correlation, the appropriate planning figure is the sum of both positions' maximum losses under the shared adverse scenario in which both resolve NO together, \(4.10+0.82=4.92\), not some smaller blended or averaged figure; positive correlation means the bad outcomes tend to occur together rather than offsetting one another, so the relevant risk-budget comparison is against this joint worst case, exactly the discipline scenario_stress and Chapter 22's bankroll material both insist on.

docs.title: Closing the book
docs.text: This book began by insisting that an event contract is not a stock, that a probability is not an oracle, and that a favorable-looking number requires evidence before it earns trust. Twenty-nine chapters and four prior practical quickstarts later, ending in this fifth and final one, that discipline has not loosened; if anything, this closing chapter has tightened it, by refusing to let even a fully truthful set of evidence declarations translate into an automatic live-trading permission. Every default example in the educational companion is synthetic, illustrative, and offline for a reason: so a reader can build every habit this book teaches, calibration discipline, cost-aware decision screens, honest no-trade outcomes, and risk budgets that bind even against a positive expected value, entirely without financial risk, before ever bringing a genuinely real dollar into contact with a genuinely real market. When that moment eventually comes, if it does, it belongs to the reader, working through Section 30.5's checks with their own current, independently verified information, not to any script in this book.

docs.title: Prediction-market book companion
docs.text: This is the isolated Python teaching project for Machine Learning for Prediction Markets, not the repository's production trading system. Its package, dependencies, data, examples, and tests are local to book\companion\.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12. Starting from the trading repository root in PowerShell:

Set-Location book\companion
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.lock
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e . --no-deps
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe examples\payoffs.py

If already in book\companion, omit the Set-Location command. Subsequent companion commands run from this directory, not the trading-system repository root. The runtime lock pins package versions, not platform-specific wheels or the build backend.

Use this project's .venv, not a virtual environment from the repository root whose editable install may still point to the former source location. The local .gitignore keeps environments, Python caches and optional snapshots out of version control without requiring production-root settings.

docs.title: Examples and data
docs.text:
The example guide covers 17 deterministic offline demonstrations. The data dictionary describes their synthetic fixtures and the optional, explicitly opted-in public snapshot collector. No default example needs accounts, credentials, paid data, a GPU, or network access after installation.

The real NOAA study reproduces its frozen forecasting results without network access or file writes:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe experiments\noaa_study.py

That study uses current/final-vintage observations and a hypothetical information clock. It has no historical prediction-market prices, fees, or fills, and is not evidence of a tradable edge. Do not rewrite or refreeze data to hide a reproduction failure.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
From the companion project directory:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -q

Manuscript checks are separate and use only the Python standard library. From the trading repository root:

python -m unittest discover -s book\tests -q
python book\scripts\assemble_claims.py --check
python book\scripts\manuscript_inventory.py

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
The companion is paper-only and its ledger is in-memory. It contains no funded-order submission, wallet signing, credential loading, or automatic promotion to live trading. Public snapshots preserve native venue fields and do not turn the classroom ledger into a venue broker.

The research standards and review records document the evidence and inspection limits. The book's final guide is a guarded manual decision checklist, not financial or legal advice or a profit guarantee.

docs.title: What is and is not included
docs.text:
fixtures\recurring_events.csv is entirely synthetic, generated for this original book. It is not downloaded, anonymized exchange data, a news archive, or an empirical prediction-market performance sample. The neighboring provenance.json records its origin. There are 180 invented events and 360 rows: two observations sharing each event's single binary outcome.

All 17 default examples are offline, deterministic teaching demonstrations. Their JSON explicitly says SYNTHETIC / ILLUSTRATIVE and live_edge_claim: false. Scores, inferred model probabilities, paper profits, bandit rewards, favorable basket calculations, and losses in those examples have no empirical market-performance interpretation.

No third-party observations, externally written bulletin, or paid-model output is used in these synthetic fixtures. Their calendar and contractual identifiers are invented. The separate real NOAA extract contains attributed government observations, and its completed experiment preserves acquisition records, frozen results, and retrospective-data limitations.

docs.title: Reproduce the environment and fixture
docs.text:
Run all commands in this guide from the companion project root, book\companion, as described in the companion setup. From the trading repository root, first run Set-Location book\companion.

The initial environment was Python 3.12.6 on Windows, CPU only. requirements.lock was generated by pip freeze --exclude prediction-market-lab after installing the declared package. It contains version-pinned runtime dependencies, not an editable absolute local path. It is a portable version lock, not a wheel/hash lock: platform wheels and floating-point library builds can differ. The build frontend/backend is not frozen by this runtime lock.

python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.lock
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e . --no-deps
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -c "from pathlib import Path; from prediction_market_lab.data import write_recurring; write_recurring(Path(r'data\fixtures\recurring_events.csv'))"
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_companion_*.py" -v
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe examples\payoffs.py

For a simpler unpinned setup, installing -e . directly from this companion directory resolves the supported dependency ranges in pyproject.toml. Use the lock when reproducing documented numerical model results.

The generator uses Python's random.Random(20260910). For each event it draws a latent value uniformly on [-1.5, 1.5], forms a logistic probability with coefficient 0.9, and draws one Bernoulli outcome. Signal noise has standard deviation 0.8 at the 12-hour horizon and 0.4 at the 3-hour horizon. The invented market forecast is 0.5 + 0.11 * signal + Gaussian(0, 0.06), bounded to [0.05, 0.95]. Recorded signal and forecast values round to six decimals. Template text describes that noisy signal, not the realized outcome. The latent probability is not offered to a fitted model as a feature.

docs.title: Recurring-event schema
docs.text:
Every timestamp is an aware UTC ISO-8601 string. All prices in this file are forecast benchmarks, not executable bids or asks.

Column Type and meaning event_id Invented realized-event identifier, toy-0000 through toy-0179. group_id Dependence-group identifier; equals event_id here. Both snapshots must stay together. family_id invented-recurring; identifies the shared synthetic template, not an additional independent label. event_time Invented event occurrence, daily at 18:00 UTC. published_at Invented bulletin publication, ten minutes before the decision. observed_at Invented local receipt, two minutes before the decision. decision_at Invented decision, twelve or three hours before the event. label_available_at Invented outcome availability, twelve hours after the event. This is not necessarily settlement time. signal Finite noisy synthetic explanatory variable. horizon_hours 12.0 or 3.0, nonnegative finite hours to the event. market_probability Invented noisy benchmark YES probability, bounded to [0.05, 0.95]. outcome One integer 0/1 label per event, repeated across snapshots. Never a fractional payout. text Original invented bulletin template, derived from available signal. synthetic Literal True; explicit provenance flag, not inferred from filenames.

EventRow.features_available() requires both publication and observation at or before the decision. grouped_chronological_split purges a whole group if it straddles a cutoff or its labels are not available at the relevant cohort cutoff. The training cutoff is April 1, the calibration cutoff May 16, and final retrospective evaluation cutoff July 1, 2025, all at 00:00 UTC. The last observation of each event is the predeclared model/scoring unit. The early snapshot is retained for temporal-update demonstrations, not counted as another independent realized event.

Model preprocessing and fitting use only the training cohort. Isotonic calibration uses only the next validation cohort; test labels are used only for retrospective scores. Isotonic output is bounded to its fitted range when inputs are out of range; evaluated probabilities are not silently clipped away from 0/1. Thus a wrong certain prediction has infinite natural log loss, rendered as the JSON string "Infinity". Small validation samples can make this happen; it is an intended lesson, not hidden by the reporter.

docs.title: Other deterministic fixtures and economics
docs.text:
The small books and user-supplied fills in examples\_support.py and the execution/market-making scripts are original in-memory fixtures. Their fixed clock is 2025-07-01T12:00:00+00:00; their identifiers and rule descriptions are not venue instruments. examples\policy_learning.py uses seed 11 for 800 training rounds and seed 12 for two 800-round comparison logs. The shared bandit generator's default seed is 20260910.

The canonical fee is an invented USD 0.01 per unit per fill, not a Kalshi or Polymarket schedule. FeeSchedule can also express an invented notional-rate component. Total fees round up to cents once per fill. Trade notional rounds half-up to cents once per fill; whole-unit quantities and four-decimal price/payout grids are classroom conventions. Separate fills can cost differently from an aggregate fill. Pending buys reserve a conservative one-unit-fill cash bound. Sales reserve owned units; naked sales, overfills and consuming another buy order's reserve are rejected. There is no assumed settlement fee; a real experiment must explicitly model any applicable one.

Taker replay consumes the finite displayed depth of an identified snapshot. Reusing the same snapshot cannot replenish its depth. A newly identified snapshot is an explicit external assertion of new observed liquidity; callers must not rename stale data to fabricate replenishment. Instantaneous taker execution is a disclosed paper assumption, not historical evidence. Resting quote touches never cause a fill. Maker fills require an explicit user-supplied synthetic event and must respect the limit and remaining size.

The ledger is single-process, in-memory and long-only, with FIFO cent cost-basis allocation. It is not a persistent production broker, concurrent matching engine, OMS, tax ledger, or venue-specific collateral model. mark requires fresh, sufficient remaining bid depth and subtracts hypothetical exit fees. A mark changes no cash, inventory, or realized profit. Fractional exceptional settlement is a payout record whose binary_label is None, not a 0.5 training target.

docs.title: Integration contract for real-data experiments
docs.text:
No default example performs network access. The separate, optional market_data module implements four allowlisted public snapshot GETs, described below. It preserves native fields instead of presenting changing fee schedules, fractional venue quantity grids or product rules as equivalent to the classroom broker. Additional real-data adapters require their own verification against current official documents. The primary indexes are https://docs.kalshi.com/llms.txt and https://docs.polymarket.com/llms.txt. The implemented scope is only the four snapshot endpoints below, not either venue's full API.

  • Keep raw-response provenance, endpoint/product, request parameters, UTC observation time, pagination and applicable permissions. Use public read-only GETs with bounded timeouts and explicit errors if acquisition is needed. Never add credential loading or funded-order capabilities here.
  • Do not label a retrieved current snapshot as a historical vintage. Price history is not a full executable order-book/fill history.
  • Use scoring.brier_score, scoring.log_loss, and scoring.calibration_bins for finite binary forecasts; report independent event counts and your weighting scheme. regression_metrics is available for a separately justified continuous target, not to blur fractional payout and binary label.
  • EventRow supports synthetic=False for honestly documented real rows, but it represents a recurring binary-event schema with one feature-publication clock. For heterogeneous sources, preserve each feature's own publication and observation times before constructing a validated row. It does not manufacture missing vintages or validate source claims.
  • grouped_chronological_split and TemporalSplit separate train, validation and retrospective test cutoffs. Dependence groups are supplied by the researcher. Broader common-shock dependence still needs an explicit inference method; grouping by event alone is not a universal cure.
  • fit_forecaster is a small preset numerical teaching pipeline, not an automated search, financial performance backtest, or guaranteed best model.
  • PaperBroker accepts only USD classroom contracts, whole quantities and explicit fills. Do not coerce incompatible real venue quantities, payout currency, fees or settlement into it without extending and testing the schema and stating the assumptions.
  • assess_evidence rejects synthetic data and missing evidence. Even if all evidence declarations are true, it returns RESEARCH_REVIEW_REQUIRED, never a live recommendation. These declarations must be independently audited; toggling booleans does not establish evidence.

docs.title: Optional public venue snapshots
docs.text:
Do not acquire or share venue data before checking applicable current terms and permissions. Public accessibility is not a redistribution license. The source audit did not establish unrestricted venue-data redistribution rights. --acknowledge-terms records an explicit user acknowledgement, not a legal eligibility determination. Access restrictions, 401/403/451 responses, unavailable books and changing schemas are reasons to stop, not to authenticate, change geographic routes or bypass controls.

The collector is separate from all 17 offline examples and from the NOAA real-data study. Nothing calls it by default, import has no network effect, and running the module without a subcommand fails before any network call. No live venue payload is committed with this implementation. Endpoint and schema documents were inspected on 2026-09-10; transport, pagination and error behavior were tested using original mocked responses, not by claiming successful live acquisition.

docs.title: Supported public GETs and native fields
docs.text:
Subcommand Exact endpoint and selected query fields Preserved response and interpretation kalshi-markets https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/markets; limit, cursor, status, optional series_ticker / event_ticker Native markets and cursor envelope, ticker/event identity, lifecycle state, market type, rules, native _dollars/_fp strings and all extra metadata. Filter status is not assumed to use the same vocabulary as returned lifecycle state. kalshi-book https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/markets/{ticker}/orderbook?depth=20 orderbook_fp.yes_dollars and .no_dollars, each containing [price_dollars, count_fp] string pairs. Both sides are bids; quantities remain fractional strings. No synthetic asks, fills or integer-unit coercions are inserted. polymarket-markets https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/markets; limit, offset, closed, fixed order=id&ascending=true Native array of Gamma market objects; IDs, questions, condition/rule metadata, collateral hints, all extra fields. clobTokenIds, outcomes and outcomePrices remain JSON-encoded strings, not reordered or silently translated into the SDK's different envelope. polymarket-book https://clob.polymarket.com/book?token_id={token_id} Native market, asset_id, timestamp, hash, bids/asks with string price/size, min_order_size, tick_size, neg_risk, last_trade_price, and extra fields. Returned asset_id must equal the requested token. Timestamp remains its native digit string.

Discovery validation checks the consumed envelope and market identity; book validation checks the consumed native decimal-string shapes and required fields. Unknown fields are preserved, not discarded. This is a small subset validator, not a claim of complete OpenAPI conformance or verification of contractual correctness. A scalar Kalshi market in metadata is retained as scalar, never turned into a binary training label.

The Polymarket endpoints are the Predictions Gamma/CLOB product, not Polymarket US, Perps, or a guarantee that a native collateral token equals cash USD. Neither collector infers fees, rounding, settlement rules, eligibility, fills or historical availability. No returned native record is converted into PaperBroker, its fee schedule, or its quantity grid.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Offline inspection and focused tests:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m prediction_market_lab.market_data --help
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m prediction_market_lab.market_data polymarket-book --help
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_companion_market_data.py" -v

Optional acquisitions, only after your independent permission checks:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m prediction_market_lab.market_data kalshi-markets --acknowledge-terms --page-size 5 --max-pages 1 --output data\local-snapshots\kalshi-markets.snapshot.json
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m prediction_market_lab.market_data polymarket-markets --acknowledge-terms --page-size 5 --max-pages 1 --output data\local-snapshots\gamma-markets.snapshot.json

$Ticker = "REPLACE-WITH-A-VERIFIED-DISCOVERED-TICKER"
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m prediction_market_lab.market_data kalshi-book --ticker $Ticker --depth 20 --acknowledge-terms --output data\local-snapshots\kalshi-book.snapshot.json

$TokenId = "REPLACE_WITH_A_VERIFIED_OUTCOME_TOKEN_ID"
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m prediction_market_lab.market_data polymarket-book --token-id $TokenId --acknowledge-terms --output data\local-snapshots\clob-book.snapshot.json

The placeholders are not real instrument identifiers and must be replaced; the token placeholder is intentionally rejected by input validation. Discovery does not automatically select a supposedly compatible contract or outcome. A selected Gamma token must be interpreted with its market's outcome list, rules and product context.

Optional common flags: --timeout 10, --max-bytes 2097152, --retries 1. Kalshi discovery supports --status open|unopened|closed|settled, --series-ticker and --event-ticker. Polymarket discovery uses closed=false by default; --closed selects closed records. These are current responses even when the records describe settled events.

Programmatic equivalent:

from prediction_market_lab.market_data import RequestPolicy, SnapshotClient

# Only run after independently checking applicable permissions.
client = SnapshotClient(
    acknowledge_terms=True,
    policy=RequestPolicy(timeout_seconds=10, retries=1),
)
snapshot = client.kalshi_markets(page_size=5, max_pages=1)

Construction without explicit acknowledge_terms=True fails. Even the standalone HTTP transport requires explicit acknowledgement. No method accepts credentials, custom headers, arbitrary endpoint roots or arbitrary HTTP methods.

docs.title: Bounds, pacing and failure semantics
docs.text:
• Defaults: 20 metadata records per page, one page, 20 Kalshi levels per side, 2 MiB per response, 10-second socket timeout, one additional attempt after a retryable failure. No polling loop or automatic book acquisition follows discovery.
  • Hard local caps: 100 records per page, 10 pages, 100 Kalshi levels per side, 4 MiB per response, 30-second socket timeout and two retries. Depth zero/unbounded Kalshi requests are refused. CLOB /book does not expose this depth parameter; its full returned body must fit the byte cap or acquisition fails rather than truncating the JSON.
  • Requests within one client are spaced at least one second apart. Retryable statuses are 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504; bounded network/socket failures can also retry. Backoff is at least one second, then two seconds. A valid Retry-After seconds value or HTTP date is honored. A malformed value, or a requested delay exceeding the default 30-second wait budget, aborts rather than retrying prematurely.
  • Timeout is applied to socket operations, with a deadline checked between bounded body chunks. It is not an OS-level hard DNS deadline. Content-Length and streamed bytes are both bounded. Compressed responses are refused after requesting identity encoding.
  • Only exact HTTPS hosts, routes and supported query parameters are accepted. All redirects are refused before a second request, including redirects to another allowed host. No cookies, authentication handler, environment proxy credentials or user-supplied headers are loaded. Direct verified-TLS connections only; networks requiring proxy configuration are unsupported, not worked around.
  • HTTP failures propagate. There is no synthetic fallback. CLI acquisition failure exits nonzero and writes no success snapshot. Library SnapshotError retains completed pages and attempt metadata in memory for inspection if a later page fails.
  • Kalshi cursors are treated as opaque query values, never URLs. Repeated cursors cause an error. Gamma uses the documented offset /markets endpoint, not the newer keyset endpoint. Full final pages at the local limit are marked possibly truncated; a short Gamma page or terminal Kalshi cursor marks that response sequence exhausted.
  • Mutable pagination is not a transactionally consistent universe. Duplicate IDs are preserved and reported; gaps remain possible. Even an exhausted traversal does not establish a complete historical dataset. A finite-depth Kalshi book separately flags omitted levels as possible.

docs.title: Saved snapshot schema and archival meaning
docs.text:
Each output is a new file ending in .snapshot.json, inside the current working directory. Existing files are not overwritten. The companion's .gitignore excludes that suffix everywhere and data\local-snapshots\ entirely. Do not force-add or redistribute snapshots without applicable permission.

The bundle contains:

  • format, classification, venue, product, endpoint, snapshot_scope: CURRENT_ONLY, historical_point_in_time: false, publication_history: UNKNOWN, and live_edge_claim: false.
  • Explicit acknowledgement plus eligibility_or_redistribution_rights_verified: false.
  • schema_reference: documented API version, official documentation URLs, inspection date and deliberately limited schema-validation scope.
  • started_at_utc, completed_at_utc, configured request_policy, and attempts recording requested URL, fixed GET method, local times, HTTP/error status and retry delay where applicable.
  • pages: exact requested URL; UTC receive time; unknown publication time; safe response metadata such as Content-Type, Date, ETag and Last-Modified; byte count; original response bytes encoded as Base64; SHA-256 of those exact bytes; parsed native payload; and a distinct SHA-256 of the sorted, compact, UTF-8 parsed JSON representation. Raw bytes are authoritative for original JSON numeric spelling. The canonical payload hash does not imply a venue signature.
  • pagination: page and record counts, configured cap, explicit truncated/more_records_possible, completion reason, continuation cursor or offset, and duplicate IDs preserved.
  • Requested Kalshi book depth, depth-truncation warning, and the explicit absence of complete book history.

Keep a source's native timestamp, local receive time, HTTP Date, Last-Modified and any metadata updatedAt separate. None automatically supplies the historical publication time of every returned field. A stored current snapshot can support a future prospective record; it does not retroactively become a historical vintage or an executable-profit record.

The Kalshi book guide explicitly describes unauthenticated public access, but the embedded endpoint OpenAPI also displayed authentication fields. The collector follows the public-GET guide without credentials and simply fails if the deployed endpoint refuses access. It never escalates to auth. The guide's array-order descriptions differ from some endpoint prose. Polymarket's narrative guide and OpenAPI examples also disagree on book array order. Therefore this collector preserves returned order and does not assume that index zero or the last index is the best executable level. These inconsistencies are disclosed rather than silently resolved into venue-trading behavior.

docs.title: NOAA observational extract: attribution and provenance
docs.text: These are real observational records, not synthetic examples or prediction-market data. The CSV preserves the source's eight numeric field tokens for January 1975 through December 2025. Only whitespace delimiters and column names were normalized. Flagged rows remain in the CSV so exclusions can be audited; the study does not treat them as observed targets or interpolate replacements.

docs.title: Provider and permitted use
docs.text:
Data provided by NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, Boulder, Colorado, USA (gml.noaa.gov), Carbon Cycle and Greenhouse Gases group, 325 Broadway R/GML, Boulder, CO 80305 (group website).

  • Monthly Mauna Loa CO2 source
  • Data documentation and citation guidance
  • NOAA GML use policy
  • Book source records: NOAA_CO2, NOAA_DATA, and NOAA_POLICY.

The documentation's current reference guidance credits Dr. Xin Lan, NOAA/GML, and Dr. Ralph Keeling, Scripps Institution of Oceanography, for the broader Trends page. This extract specifically acknowledges NOAA-period measurements; the book authors are not the measurement creators.

The inspected government-data policy permits public use unless specifically annotated otherwise and requires acknowledgement, no implied NOAA endorsement, and no presentation of modified material as official government information. The incorporated NOAA observations are U.S. government data not subject to the book's original-content copyright. NOAA supplies them without warranty. Normalization, derived binary labels, forecasts, and figures are the book authors' transformations, not official NOAA products. NOAA does not endorse this book or its models.

The source identifies March 1958-April 1974 as Scripps data. Its third-party status must not be erased by generalizing the government-data policy. The conservative January 1975 boundary excludes those observations, as well as May-December 1974. No complete 1958-onward raw response is redistributed.

docs.title: Exact normalized CSV schema
docs.text:
Column, in order Meaning year Integer observation year month Integer calendar month, 1-12 decimal_date Source decimal year; not a publication/availability timestamp average Recorded monthly mean CO2, ppm deseasonalized Source adjusted CO2, ppm; preserved for provenance, never used as a predictor ndays Integer contributing days; nonpositive is unusable sdev Daily standard deviation, ppm; negative is an unavailable/interpolation flag uncertainty Monthly-mean uncertainty, ppm; negative is an unavailable/interpolation flag

All numeric fields must be finite. Dates must be valid, unique, and strictly ordered; the extract must contain every calendar record in the fixed interval. Monthly record completeness does not mean that every row is valid for a target. Missing/nonpositive concentrations and source flags invalidate any event depending on that source month. December 1975 has nonpositive ndays and negative sdev; April 1984 has negative sdev. Flags are checked independently, not only when multiple flag columns agree.

docs.title: Availability, location, and scientific limits
docs.text:
This is the current/final vintage at acquisition, not archived first releases. NOAA says quality-control revisions can change the series. Monthly means include center-of-month correction, and some source records are interpolated. These properties survive a chronological split. The retained average is not a raw sensor reading or a verified historical as-of value.

The source reports alternate Maunakea measurement during December 2022-July 4, 2023. The sensitivity removes full December 2022-July 2023 source months and every target pair depending on them: December 2022-August 2023 target events.

See experiments/README.md for the predeclared clock, commands, scores, exclusions, and limitations. This dataset does not contain contracts, market prices, fees, order books, fills, or settlement publication times and cannot establish executable trading profit.

docs.title: Offline companion examples and public API
docs.text: Every executable example in this directory is original, deterministic, offline and synthetic/illustrative. None reports empirical prediction-market alpha. Every default stdout stream is a single JSON object with live_edge_claim: false. Decimal cash is serialized as strings, timestamps as aware UTC ISO-8601, and nonfinite scoring results as explicit strings such as "Infinity", not invalid JSON numeric constants.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
From the companion project root, book\companion, after the setup in the companion README:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe examples\payoffs.py
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_companion_*.py" -v

Get-ChildItem examples\*.py |
    Where-Object { -not $_.Name.StartsWith("_") } |
    ForEach-Object {
        .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe $_.FullName
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Example failed: $($_.Name)" }
    }

The targeted unittest command covers the companion modules and optional collector. Manuscript integrity checks live separately under book\tests. The companion command runs every one of the 17 example scripts in a fresh Python process with socket connection methods blocked. The small helper _support.py only constructs invented fixtures; shared accounting, fitting, scoring and decision logic live in the package.

docs.title: Optional public snapshots: separate from every default example
docs.text:
Help performs no network request:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m prediction_market_lab.market_data --help
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m prediction_market_lab.market_data kalshi-markets --help
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_companion_market_data.py" -v

After independently checking applicable terms, geographic/product access and permissions, an explicitly opted-in user can run a small current-only metadata acquisition:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m prediction_market_lab.market_data kalshi-markets --acknowledge-terms --page-size 5 --max-pages 1 --output data\local-snapshots\kalshi-markets.snapshot.json
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m prediction_market_lab.market_data polymarket-markets --acknowledge-terms --page-size 5 --max-pages 1 --output data\local-snapshots\gamma-markets.snapshot.json

These are optional network commands, not commands run by the book's default examples or tests. They do not place orders. The acknowledgement is not proof of legal eligibility or permission to redistribute. Outputs must be new local files ending in .snapshot.json, which Git ignores.

The other subcommands are kalshi-book --ticker <verified-ticker> and polymarket-book --token-id <verified-outcome-token-id>, with the same required acknowledgement and output flags. No identifier is automatically selected for you. Full request examples, checked official schemas, retry rules, native-field provenance and limits are in the optional snapshot documentation. Do not pass these native venue records into PaperBroker.

docs.text:

docs.title: Limitations and downstream real-data work
docs.text:
See the data dictionary and integration contract before using any model or schema with real observations. Particularly:

  • Current snapshots cannot reconstruct earlier feature vintages or executable depth. A real collector must be independently checked against current official APIs and keep raw-response provenance.
  • The only optional network module, market_data, is an explicitly gated public-snapshot collector. The default examples never invoke it. No credential loading, funded-order endpoint, wallet signing or live switch exists.
  • Ledger reconciliation is an internal consistency check, not exchange reconciliation; the ledger is not persisted across Python processes.
  • Synthetic maker events and instantaneous taker fills are explicit assumptions. No empirical fill rate, queue model, cancellation latency, alpha, fee schedule or profitability claim is supplied.
  • Fractional Kelly, joint-scenario stress, manually supplied compatibility and boolean evidence declarations are teaching interfaces, not automatic verification of real contracts or a sufficient investment process.
  • Real-data researchers can directly reuse the score functions. Adapting EventRow or PaperBroker to richer metadata, venue collateral, fractional quantities and actual costs requires explicit validation and new tests; do not silently coerce incompatible data.

docs.title: Real NOAA data: a frozen probability-forecasting study
docs.text:
Retrospective FINAL-VINTAGE teaching exercise, not a prediction-market backtest, an issued-forecast archive, or profitability evidence.

The question is whether a target-calendar-month event rate improves on an expanding overall rate when forecasting whether the recorded monthly CO2 mean is strictly greater than the immediately preceding calendar month's mean. Ties are NO. Both means are needed to define the eventual outcome; neither mean is used as a predictor. Models use only calendar information and labels already admitted under the hypothetical clock below.

The real data are attributed NOAA GML measurements. See the data attribution and schema, provenance, and research feasibility assessment. No source-book code or text is used.

docs.title: Reproduce offline
docs.text:
Run these PowerShell commands from the companion project root, book\companion, after the documented installation. The study reuses prediction_market_lab.scoring.brier_score, log_loss, and calibration_bins. It adds no dependencies or environment changes.

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe experiments\noaa_study.py
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest tests.test_noaa_study -v

The default study command makes no network request and no file writes. It validates the CSV and provenance, verifies frozen data/protocol/implementation/ shared-scoring hashes, recomputes predictions and summaries, and compares the exact bytes with the existing outputs. Missing data, changed inputs/results, schema errors, or insufficient training history fail explicitly. There is no synthetic fallback.

The script's public CLI is deliberately small:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe experiments\noaa_study.py --help

docs.title: Acquisition and first freeze: commands actually used
docs.text:
The protocol was written before acquisition or inspecting either model's scores, at 2026-09-10T21:45:25Z. This is a local predeclaration, not an external preregistration. The first acquisition and first evaluation used:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe experiments\noaa_study.py --refresh-data
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest tests.test_noaa_study.NOAAParserTests tests.test_noaa_study.NOAAClockTests tests.test_noaa_study.NOAAAcquisitionTests -v
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe experiments\noaa_study.py --freeze-results

The explicit acquisition contacts only the fixed public NOAA HTTPS URL. It rejects redirects, non-200 responses, malformed content, and responses over 2,000,000 bytes; network operations use a 30-second socket timeout. It hashes the raw response in memory and writes only the selected 1975-2025 observations and provenance. It does not evaluate scores or replace frozen results.

Acquisition completed at 2026-09-10T21:48:07Z. The source's exact original creation string was Sat Sep 5 03:55:38 2026, with no specified timezone. The first and single frozen evaluation was persisted at 2026-09-10T21:49:19Z.

On this shipped checkout, acquisition or freezing without replacement flags refuses to overwrite existing artifacts. To deliberately replace a dataset or reviewed evaluation, the distinct explicit opt-ins are:

# Maintenance only: these are NOT the reproduction commands.
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe experiments\noaa_study.py --refresh-data --replace-data
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe experiments\noaa_study.py --freeze-results --replace-results

These flags do not alter protocol.json. A refreshed source may have revisions; existing frozen results will then fail verification until explicitly replaced. Do not use replacement to select favorable results. Preserve the prior tracked artifacts in version history before intentional maintenance. The shipped frozen-data regression test pins the original extract hash; replacing a changed extract intentionally requires reviewing that test and all quoted book results. Parameter changes require a new reviewed protocol/implementation, not silently editing version 1. Exact-byte verification is intentionally strict: even a reviewed scoring implementation change requires inspecting and explicitly accepting a replacement run.

Scoped .gitattributes rules disable Git line-ending normalization for hashed study/data artifacts and the shared scoring.py. The initial source files include CRLF endings while generated data use LF; forcing all files to LF would change the frozen hashes on a new checkout. Preserving the original bytes avoids that change without rewriting the protocol or rerunning a selected evaluation. A formatting-only change still trips the explicit implementation-review gate. The Git-filter regression locates the actual Git checkout root independently of this nested Python project, so it checks the same byte-preserving attributes whether the companion is nested or checked out on its own.

docs.title: Predeclared protocol
docs.text:
protocol.json is the authoritative design. Its SHA-256 is 3ce89596a3bfa3fa12a2b30f116f473fc000a827623b4011839fd3d33f5f5e71.

  • Source window: January 1975-December 2025, 612 calendar records.
  • Evaluation: January 2015-December 2025, fixed before scores; expanding training rather than a model fitted once and left unchanged.
  • Valid event: two truly consecutive, valid calendar-month observations. No shifting across deleted rows; no interpolation.
  • Clock: the label for target month s is admitted at 00:00 UTC on the first day of month s+2. A forecast at the start of target month t uses target labels no later than t-2. Thus the January 2015 forecast can use labels through November 2014; December 2014 is not yet admitted.
  • Initial history: 1975-2014 records provide 475 pre-evaluation events, of which 474 are admitted for January 2015. At least 36 admitted labels are required for every forecast; failure is an error, not silently dropping an evaluation month. Later evaluation labels enter training only after their hypothetical admission dates.
  • Overall baseline: add one to the admitted YES count and divide by the admitted count plus two, the Beta(1,1) posterior predictive mean.
  • Seasonal model: use the same smoothing but only admitted labels with the target's calendar month. The month is the target month, not the prior observation's month. No pooling or tuning.
  • Forbidden inputs: contemporaneous/target CO2 levels, deseasonalized values, labels not yet admitted, and transformations fitted after cutoff.
  • Scoring: one equally weighted squared YES-probability error per event for Brier score; natural-log loss. No endpoint clipping. Wrong zero-probability forecasts have infinite log loss in the core; Beta smoothing keeps these particular forecasts strictly inside zero and one.
  • Difference: seasonal score minus overall score; negative favors seasonal.
  • Inference: descriptive scores and fixed five-bin calibration summaries, no p-values or confidence intervals. Eleven years of dependent monthly events do not justify an independent-row uncertainty claim.

The clock is an explicitly hypothetical retrospective index convention, not evidence of actual historical publication or local observation times. The final-vintage data limitation is not fixed by lagging labels.

docs.title: Actual exclusions and counts
docs.text:
The extract has 612 calendar rows, 610 valid source records, and 607 usable target events across all years. Five calendar targets are excluded:

Target Reason January 1975 No December 1974 predecessor in the conservative extract December 1975 Target source record: nonpositive days and negative standard deviation January 1976 Previous source record has those flags April 1984 Target source record: negative standard deviation May 1984 Previous source record has that flag

None of these exclusions falls in the primary evaluation. It contains 132 monthly events, twelve in each of eleven years, with 85 YES outcomes (rate 0.643939394). The overall admitted-label count ranges from 474 to 605; the seasonal model has 38-50 same-calendar-month admitted labels per forecast.

The sensitivity conservatively excludes full December 2022-July 2023 source months affected by alternate measurement location. Every event depending on an affected target or predecessor is removed from both training and evaluation. This excludes December 2022-August 2023 targets, nine events, leaving 123 evaluation events with 79 YES outcomes (rate 0.642276423). August is excluded because its July predecessor is affected; September remains eligible. The reduced cohort has eleven 2022 events and four 2023 events, with twelve in each other evaluation year. Both models are refitted using the same remaining admitted labels and scored on this same reduced cohort.

docs.text:
Lower is better for both scores. All numbers below are descriptive and rounded for display; the report and prediction files retain full floating-point values.
