To separate removal of events from refitting effects, the predeclared report also scores the original primary forecasts on the same 123-event sensitivity cohort. On that matched cohort, without refitting, overall/seasonal Brier scores are 0.230747205 / 0.034717811, and log losses are 0.654233669 / 0.137703440. Those are a cohort diagnostic, not an additional model selected after evaluation.

The original SVG uses the verified report, not a second fit or evaluation selection. Nonempty calibration bins show their monthly event counts. It can be regenerated offline with the standard library; no plotting dependency was added:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe experiments\render_noaa_figure.py

This separate rendering command writes the SVG asset; the default study command continues to write nothing. The figure is descriptive and has no uncertainty bands. Source data, modeling transformations, and the no-endorsement boundary remain labeled.

The simple seasonal model has lower scores in this frozen descriptive comparison. Recurring seasonality is useful for this particular recorded-rise target. That observation does not show that either probability is calibrated in another domain, beats market prices, or can support a profitable trade.

docs.title: Files, row schema, and verification
docs.text:
File Role noaa_study.py Explicit acquisition; parsing/validation; hypothetical clock; shared-core scoring; frozen verification protocol.json Versioned predeclaration, never rewritten by the CLI ../data/real/noaa_co2_monthly_1975_2025.csv Filtered, attributed real observations including flags ../data/real/provenance.json Actual retrieval and source metadata, schema, hashes, counts results/predictions.csv Exactly one primary forecast row per usable evaluation month results/sensitivity_predictions.csv Exactly one refitted sensitivity row per comparable month results/report.json Counts, exclusions, model definitions, scores, probability ranges, fixed-bin calibration, matched-cohort diagnostic, limitations results/frozen_run.json Actual freeze time and input/output hash bindings render_noaa_figure.py Standard-library rendering of a verified report; no additional fitting assets/noaa_calibration_scores.svg Original accessible SVG, not a NOAA-produced or endorsed figure ../tests/test_noaa_study.py Stdlib unittest checks, including a real offline subprocess invocation

Prediction CSV columns identify target/previous months, UTC hypothetical forecast/label-admission timestamps, eventual binary label, training cutoff, latest admitted target, overall and seasonal training/YES counts, both probabilities, both per-event Brier/log losses, and per-event paired differences. Each event is present once within its cohort; repeated monthly snapshots are not counted as independent observations.

Tests verify gaps and ties, flags independently, invalid dates, duplicates and ordering, exact eight-field schemas, finite values, response limits/errors, admission at s+2, invariance to changing unadmitted/future labels, explicit insufficient-history errors, frozen hashes/counts, shared score agreement, replacement gates, tampered inputs/results, and actual offline reproduction without network or writes. The small hand-constructed records in unit tests test edge cases; they are not used in the empirical results.

docs.title: What this study cannot establish
docs.text:
1. Point-in-time validity: the source is a mutable current/final-vintage series, not a historical release archive. Revisions and provider processing can affect threshold labels. Even the average column includes center-of- month correction; avoiding the deseasonalized column is necessary but not sufficient to reconstruct historical knowledge.
  2. Historical availability: the study has no verified original publication timestamps. The hypothetical lag teaches an admission discipline rather than proving data were available at a past decision time.
  3. Market forecast quality: there are no historical event contracts or market prices to compare with either model.
  4. Profitability or execution: there are no spreads, fees, collateral, orders, fills, latency, queues, or settlement rules. No P&L is computed.
  5. Generalization or certainty: observed seasonality and eleven evaluation years cannot establish an edge in unrelated event markets. There is no independent-month significance claim and no guaranteed future performance.
  6. A live-trade permission gate: this experiment is not passing evidence for the first-live-trade guide. Real money, eligibility, and operational verification remain separate questions.

docs.title: Evidence foundation
docs.text: This directory supports an original book, not a derivative reconstruction of another textbook. No source-book repository, chapter prose, or paper PDF is included.

docs.title: Files and roles
docs.text:
• sources.json: canonical citation IDs, exact bibliographic identity where verified, inspection depth, supported uses, and explicit boundaries.
  • claims.csv: aggregate claim-to-source map assembled from the source audit and chapter fragments. It is not a claim that every manuscript sentence has been formally proved.
  • claim-fragments/foundation.csv: the foundational source audit, retained separately from the authors' chapter claims.
  • data-feasibility.md: a concrete real-data recommendation, provenance and rights assessment, and the limits of venue acquisition.
  • ../references.md: reader-facing bibliography with stable ## ID anchors.

docs.title: How to use evidence
docs.text:
Read verification, supports, and limitations together. The ledger distinguishes:

  1. Relevant full-text sections inspected: the named sections were read; this is not a claim that every proof, experiment, supplement, or later revision was checked.
  2. Primary abstract and metadata inspected: claims must stay within the inspected abstract unless an author independently inspects and records additional text.
  3. Publisher-deposited registry metadata: bibliographic identity was checked against Crossref's publisher-deposited DOI record, sometimes supplemented by an institutional page. This is not a reading of the paper. A metadata-only record is a qualified reading pointer, not substantive empirical evidence.
  4. Official documentation inspected: the named content was read from the operator or data provider. It describes the retrieved document, not a historical version or a permanent operational promise.
  5. Partial official response: access or operative terms remain incomplete; do not upgrade this into verified eligibility or reuse permission.

The explicit registry fallback matters. Several publisher interfaces denied access or returned only citation controls. Follow-up inspection recovered author manuscripts and primary abstracts for ten initially metadata-only records; three remain qualified bibliographic pointers. Rather than invent full-text verification, the bibliography records that boundary. Sources with only metadata should not be used as the sole support for a detailed theorem, numeric result, or operational recommendation. The claim map favors actually inspected abstracts, relevant article sections, actual documentation, and explicitly independent derivations.

docs.title: Citation and claim contract
docs.text:
Use [WZ2006](../references.md#wz2006) from chapters. Keys are stable and case-sensitive in JSON; Markdown anchors are lowercase. Multiple sources in CSV use semicolon-separated IDs. locator identifies the actually inspected abstract, section, or documentation heading rather than fabricating a page or theorem number.

After reviewing changed fragments, rebuild the aggregate from the trading repository root with python book\scripts\assemble_claims.py; use python book\scripts\assemble_claims.py --check for a read-only consistency check. The assembler rejects malformed records, duplicate claim identifiers, missing limitations, and unknown source keys. It does not decide whether a paper actually supports a statement; that remains a source-reading and editorial task.

Evidence types distinguish theoretical_abstract, empirical_abstract, method_abstract, full_text_section, official_documentation, and data_provenance. A source paper's proof or benchmark is not a prediction-market profitability result. Derived classroom identities, synthetic demonstrations, and untested hypotheses should be labeled as such rather than dressed up with unrelated citations.

A paper published in a journal may have an earlier working paper or a later repository upload. Keep the publication year distinct from upload date: the Bailey journal article is 2017; the Gelman journal article is 2008 despite a 2009 arXiv deposit; the Hanson journal issue is 2007 despite later web metadata. Manski's NBER working paper is cited as that version, not silently as a later journal article.

docs.title: Stable citation IDs by topic
docs.text:
Topic IDs Price interpretation and empirical market forecasting WZ2006, MANSKI2004, WZ2004, BERG2008 Market scoring and combinatorial mechanism design HANSON2007, ABERNETHY2013 Proper scoring and calibration GNEITING2007, BRIER1950, MURPHY1973, GUO2017, NICULESCU2005, KULL2017 Logistic models, regularization and Bayesian priors FRIEDMAN2010, TIBSHIRANI1996, GELMAN2008 Trees and boosting BREIMAN2001, FRIEDMAN2001, CHEN2016 Survival, state updates and changepoints COX1972, KALMAN1960, ADAMS2007 Text and neural foundations MANNING2008, RUMELHART1986, HOCHREITER1997, ATTENTION2017, DEVLIN2019 Forecast combinations and domain transfer BATES1969, GNEITING2013, YAO2018, GANIN2016 Selection, multiple testing and dependent/sequential inference BAILEY2017, WHITE2000, BENJAMINI1995, POLITIS1994, HOWARD2021 Growth sizing and stock-market microstructure analogies KELLY1956, GLOSTEN1985, KYLE1985, AVELLANEDA2008 Policy evaluation and offline RL limitations DUDIK2011, FUJIMOTO2019 Kalshi mechanics KALSHI_DEMO, KALSHI_HISTORY, KALSHI_BOOK, KALSHI_ROUNDING, KALSHI_SETTLEMENT Polymarket mechanics and partial terms response POLYMARKET_FEES, POLYMARKET_RESOLUTION, POLYMARKET_COLLATERAL, POLYMARKET_BOOK, POLYMARKET_MARKETS, POLYMARKET_TERMS Real-data provenance and permission NOAA_CO2, NOAA_DATA, NOAA_POLICY

The following three records remain bibliographic pointers, not substantively inspected original-source evidence: BRIER1950, MURPHY1973, and FRIEDMAN2001. Retain their verified identity for further reading, but independently derive elementary teaching examples or inspect additional source text before attaching detailed claims. AMS requests for Brier/Murphy remained inaccessible, the legacy NOAA archive hostname did not resolve, and Friedman retrieval encountered publisher failure, a retired hostname, and an expired author-site TLS certificate. Authentication, certificate verification, and access controls were not bypassed.

docs.title: Follow-up source inspection
docs.text:
The following upgrades were completed on the same audit date. The record of reading depth is deliberately narrower than a claim to have checked every paper in full.

ID Directly inspected material Editorial boundary GNEITING2007 Washington author copy: abstract; Section 1; Section 2.1 definitions; Section 2.3; Sections 3.1-3.2, including categorical examples and representation. Scores are positively oriented in the source; this book uses losses. Its categorical Brier sum is twice the single-YES convention. Strict propriety is an expectation property; normalized skill scores require care. KELLY1956 All ten pages, 917-926, of the permission-marked Princeton-hosted reproduction. Independent symbols/noise, reinvestment and stake control matter. The conclusion's comparison is against fixed allocations per received symbol, not every adaptive policy. No finite-horizon or estimated-probability safety guarantee. AVELLANEDA2008 NYU author copy: main text, Sections 1-3, pp. 217-223; model, approximate equations 29-30 and simulation comparison. Arithmetic Brownian stock price, exponential utility and Poisson arrival model; simple quotes are approximate. Inventory-focused, not a complete adverse-selection model. Simulation and terminal midpoint marking are not executable historical profits. GLOSTEN1985 Milgrom's Stanford-hosted reprint, visually read PDF pp. 1-3: abstract and opening introduction. Informational spread with competitive risk-neutral zero-profit pricing and no binding inventory/cash constraint. A stock-market analogy; formal proofs beyond the inspected introduction were not read. WHITE2000 Wisconsin-hosted article: abstract/opening p. 1097; Section 2a-2b through p. 1104. Candidate-family maximum versus benchmark; stationary strong-mixing data, asymptotic regularity and dependent block resampling. No cure for undocumented search, leakage or incorrect execution accounting. NICULESCU2005 Cornell author copy, PDF pp. 1-3 and 8: methods, dataset/design context and conclusions. Calibration samples independent of base fitting; model/sample-dependent benefits and harms. Random-sample benchmarks do not replace chronological event-group validation. RUMELHART1986 Hinton's Toronto copy, visually read pp. 533-535, including equations 1-9 and the local-minimum discussion. Chain-rule derivatives and gradient updates, not global optimization, historical priority, calibration or market-performance guarantees. POLITIS1994 Complete primary publisher abstract; author publication listing. Weakly dependent stationary observations and geometric block lengths; original full proof and a suitable event-data block length were not audited. BATES1969 Complete primary publisher abstract in the page's structured data. Airline-passenger point-forecast combination can lower mean-square error; not a universal probability-calibration result. KYLE1985 Complete primary Econometric Society abstract in raw HTML. One risk-neutral insider, noise traders and competitive risk-neutral market makers; continuous-limit equilibrium properties are not empirical event-market laws.

GNEITING2007 now supplies directly inspected core scoring definitions and the categorical Brier/log-score examples, so the two inaccessible historical scoring papers do not leave elementary scoring theory citation-only. No such substitution is mislabeled as a reading of Brier's or Murphy's original article.

Extraction used the already installed system Python/PyMuPDF, without modifying the companion environment or installing dependencies. PDFs were processed in memory and not saved. A small set of local rendered images was used to inspect scanned pages and removed after inspection. Only original summaries, locators, source URLs and claim boundaries are retained; no paper text or figures are redistributed.

docs.title: Audit date and change control
docs.text:
All retrievals recorded here use 2026-09-10. This is the audit's access date, not evidence of a site's past contents. No historical source snapshots, copyrighted full texts, or paper PDFs are redistributed. Mutable official documentation must be rechecked before any implementation relies on it.

Important factual corrections from direct inspection:

  • Kalshi provides a mock-funds demo and explicitly warns against treating its behavior as live-market behavior.
  • Kalshi history is split by moving cutoffs; its inspected historical-data guide does not establish a complete order-book archive.
  • Polymarket fees are market-specific, and official materials distinguish pUSD collateral from USDC-related fee/funding descriptions.
  • Polymarket resolution can involve disputes, clarifications, and a 50/50 payout.
  • An accessible website is not an unrestricted data license or permission for every reader to trade.
  • NOAA's CO2 source is real observational data but current-vintage, partly historically third-party, and not an issued-forecast or prediction-market dataset.

The strongest supported implementation path is an offline, reproducible forecast-scoring study on an attributed NOAA-period extract, with its current-vintage limitation prominently retained. Venue collection is a separate, permission-gated read-only path, and no source in this ledger alone proves a profitable trading strategy.

docs.title: Data feasibility and an honest real-data study
docs.text:
Evidence inspected on 2026-09-10. This is a feasibility assessment, not a finding of a profitable market strategy. Public accessibility, permission to redistribute, point-in-time availability, and executable trading history are four different questions.

The recommended study is now implemented in the frozen experiment. This document retains the acquisition and study-design rationale; actual retrieval records, exclusions, measured scores, and reproduction commands live with that experiment rather than being implied by this earlier feasibility work.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use a small, attributed NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory monthly Mauna Loa carbon-dioxide dataset for a reproducible, retrospective probability-forecasting study. Do not represent it as historical prediction-market data, an archive of issued forecasts, a reconstruction of information available to traders, or an executable-profit backtest.

This audit did not establish a small, redistributable, complete point-in-time prediction-market order-book dataset. Official venue APIs are useful acquisition interfaces, but an interface is not a redistribution license and a historical price series is not a historical order book.

docs.title: Concrete downstream data contract
docs.text:
Primary data URL:

https://gml.noaa.gov/webdata/ccgg/trends/co2/co2_mm_mlo.txt

Documentation: https://gml.noaa.gov/ccgg/trends/data.html

Use policy: https://gml.noaa.gov/about/disclaimer.html

The text response was successfully inspected. Its header identified file creation as 2026-09-05 03:55:38; the header did not specify a timezone, so do not silently append Z. This is a mutable current file, not a promised permanent historical version. The file's calendar records start in March 1958. No data download or study result is implied by this document; the experiment implementation must record its actual acquisition and output.

Noncomment rows contain eight whitespace-delimited fields:

Field Type Meaning and caution year integer Observation year, not publication year. month integer, 1-12 Observation month, not an as-of timestamp. decimal_date decimal Source-provided fractional year; retain rather than infer availability from it. average decimal Monthly mean CO2, in parts per million. deseasonalized decimal Source-adjusted series; exclude from predictive features in the proposed study. ndays integer Days contributing to the monthly statistic; negative values are flags, not counts. sdev decimal Standard deviation of days; negative values flag unavailable/interpolated information. uncertainty decimal Uncertainty of monthly mean; negative values flag unavailable/interpolated information.

Keep the provider's original values and names in a raw schema; use the names above only in a documented normalized schema. Skip lines beginning with #, reject non-eight-field rows, reject duplicate or out-of-order months, validate numeric fields, and record all exclusions.

docs.title: Rights and attribution
docs.text:
NOAA GML's policy states that government-server information is public domain unless specifically annotated otherwise; it permits public use subject to attribution, no implied NOAA endorsement, and no presentation of modified material as official government information. It separately warns about third-party material.

The dataset header explicitly identifies March 1958-April 1974 as Scripps Institution of Oceanography data. Do not assume the NOAA government-work statement independently licenses those third-party records. Select January 1975-December 2025 for this book's compact NOAA-period study. This is a conservative provenance boundary, not a legal determination about Scripps data.

Attribute the extracted observations to NOAA GML, Carbon Cycle and Greenhouse Gases group. Identify them as U.S. government data not covered by the book's original-content copyright. Label normalized data and derived targets as the book authors' transformations, not official NOAA products. Preserve the source URL, access time, source creation string, filtering rule, raw-content hash, extract hash, row count, and source citation in the data manifest. Consult the provider's current citation guidance; do not invent a dataset DOI or list the book authors as the measurement creators.

docs.title: Scientific and availability qualifications
docs.text:
• This is a current-vintage retrospective series. The documentation says values can change following quality-control checks. A date-ordered split cannot recover historical vintages.
  • Monthly means are corrected to the center of the month using a seasonal cycle. Even the average column should not be assumed to be an untouched first release.
  • The header says missing months have been interpolated and, for NOAA data, negative standard deviation and uncertainty identify these cases. Do not use interpolated rows as if observed. Exclude targets or features depending on flagged months, and preserve calendar gaps rather than shifting the next retained row into the missing month's place.
  • Measurement at Mauna Loa was suspended after the November 2022 eruption and resumed in July 2023. The header identifies December 2022-July 4, 2023 observations as coming from Maunakea, approximately 21 miles away. Record this location discontinuity and report a sensitivity analysis excluding the affected period if performed.
  • The deseasonalized column is especially inappropriate as an allegedly as-of feature without vintage documentation. Its omission does not turn the remaining final-vintage study into a point-in-time study.
  • No source publication-time history, market contract, executable quote, fee history, or queue data has been established for these observations.

docs.title: Companion integration boundary
docs.text: Reuse the companion's scoring functions with explicitly constructed binary targets, but do not force this revised NOAA archive into EventRow by inventing publication/observation clocks or a market-probability benchmark. The companion data contract and public API guide describe the supported interfaces. A calendar-chronological retrospective split is not a verified point-in-time split. Keep point-in-time, execution-history and cost evidence unverified, and reject any inference of a supported live edge.

docs.title: Predeclared teaching question
docs.text:
Can a simple seasonal probability model improve on an expanding overall event rate when predicting whether next month's recorded monthly mean exceeds this month's recorded monthly mean?

This is a proposed forecasting study, not a statement that the implementation has already run or that a favorable result exists.

  1. Freeze the selected real-data extract before comparing model performance. Keep January 1975-December 2025 as the intended window; disclose actual exclusions and usable event count.
  2. Define one event per calendar target month: the recorded monthly mean is strictly greater than the immediately preceding month's mean. Ties count as NO. Only consecutive, valid monthly observations qualify.
  3. Use a fixed early chronological training period and later chronological evaluation period, or expanding-origin evaluation with a prespecified minimum training span. The experiment must state exact dates before inspecting competing scores.
  4. Compare an expanding overall rate with a month-of-year seasonal frequency model, using prespecified smoothing. If logistic regression is added, train all coefficients and preprocessing only on preceding rows and do not tune on evaluation outcomes.
  5. State that the information clock is a retrospective index convention, not a verified historical publication clock. A hypothetical one-month availability lag can illustrate disciplined coding, but cannot prove that these values were actually available then.
  6. Score one forecast per target month using the book's single-YES Brier score and natural-log loss. Show base rates, sample counts, probability ranges, and the paired score difference. Treat zero/one predictions explicitly.
  7. Dependence and seasonal structure matter. If uncertainty intervals are reported, document the dependence model and block length; do not bootstrap monthly rows independently and call that a universal guarantee. A descriptive paired score difference without an interval is acceptable.
  8. Report an unfavorable or inconclusive comparison unchanged. No P&L calculation belongs in the empirical output unless clearly separated as an invented contract illustration.

The useful lesson is distinguishing strong recurring structure, credible forecast scoring, and unavailable trading evidence. This dataset does not test the relative quality of market prices, prove the transferability of a climate model to event contracts, or establish a tradable edge.

docs.title: Read-only venue acquisition: a separate future study
docs.text: The companion's classroom OrderBook, FeeSchedule and PaperBroker are not native venue representations. Their documented whole-unit quantities, four-decimal USD price/payout grid, and invented cent-rounded per-fill fees must not be confused with Kalshi fractional count_fp quantities or its order-level fee accumulator, nor with Polymarket collateral and market-specific fees. Optional public snapshot acquisition documented in data/README.md preserves native fields separately; a returned snapshot is not a verified conversion into the classroom broker. Actual quantity, collateral, rules, fee and execution adapters require separate validation.

docs.title: Kalshi
docs.text:
Start from https://docs.kalshi.com/llms.txt, then inspect the current API-environment, historical-data, pagination, rate-limit, order-book, market-rule, and fee documentation. The inspected historical-data page partitions records using GET /historical/cutoff; market settlement and trade creation use different cutoff fields. Query the appropriate live and historical interfaces rather than assuming the live interface holds every past record.

The inspected current order-book guide documents GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook, with orderbook_fp.yes_dollars and orderbook_fp.no_dollars arrays. Each level contains string-valued dollar price and fixed-point quantity. The arrays contain bids; ordinary binary opposite-side bids imply asks. Preserve size and units. The current guide gives the public base root https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2. Recheck these details before implementing a collector.

The historical endpoints listed in the inspected guide cover markets, candlesticks, trades, and relevant account records. They do not establish a complete historical order-book or queue archive. Account fills are not a substitute for all traders' order histories. A candle or trade alone cannot establish that an unplaced resting order would have filled.

Kalshi does have a separate mock-funds demo. Its official warning says demo price and behavior may not reflect real markets. Separate credentials and demo testing do not establish live execution fidelity.

docs.title: Polymarket
docs.text:
Start from https://docs.polymarket.com/llms.txt. Identify the exact product and outcome-token IDs. The inspected prices/order-books documentation exposes public CLOB reads such as https://clob.polymarket.com/book?token_id=..., with price/size arrays, book timestamp, state hash, minimum order size, and tick size. Preserve source timestamps and independently recorded receive timestamps. A state hash identifies a returned book state; it is not proof of complete history.

Do not assume zero fees. The inspected fee guide describes market-dependent taker fees and a price-dependent calculation. Its USDC fee descriptions coexist with a pUSD collateral/settlement guide: identify the actual unit and product rather than collapsing them into cash dollars. Resolution documentation permits an exceptional 50/50 payout and discusses rule clarifications after trading starts. Preserve rule versions and payout vectors rather than forcing every settlement into a binary label.

The inspected polymarket.com/tos response displayed a U.S. trading block and a link to the separate polymarket.us product. It did not expose complete operative terms in the returned text. This is not a verified all-countries eligibility matrix or a legal opinion about the U.S. product.

docs.title: Permission gate and minimum archival schema
docs.text:
No unrestricted venue-data redistribution license was established in this audit. The attempted Kalshi terms page returned a rate-limit response; complete operative Polymarket terms were not readable in the retrieved page. Unknown rights remain unknown. Do not redistribute venue payloads or assert that their public API availability supplies permission. Obtain and record the applicable current terms or permission before any substantial acquisition, sharing, or deployment. Never bypass geographic or account restrictions.

For an authorized, read-only prospective collector, retain: venue and product; series/event/market/outcome IDs; contract wording and rules hash; collateral and payout convention; venue event time; source publication time where available; local receive time; schema/version; bid/ask levels with quantities; tick and quantity grids; fee parameters with effective times; trading status; pagination cursor and collection gaps; request/retry log; and final payout plus its publication/settlement times. Store no credentials in datasets.

A future execution study additionally needs a defensible fill model, latency and cancellation records, queue assumptions, and a held-out evaluation protocol. Where these are missing, narrow the conclusion to observed forecasting or market-description evidence and retain a no-trade result.

docs.title: Review scope and interpretation
docs.text:
The review process separates technical correctness from whole-manuscript editing. It is an internal quality-control process, not academic peer review, a legal opinion, or certification that a strategy is profitable.

Technical review should inspect derivations, empirical claims, source support, information availability, accounting, statistical selection, execution assumptions, and the boundary between hypothetical, synthetic, historical, and actual results. It should compare the executable examples to the text rather than treating successful execution as evidence that the underlying model is true.

Editorial review should read the complete ordered manuscript and its supporting notation, glossary, references, and exercise material. It should address contradictions between chapters, missing prerequisites, terminology changes, duplicated explanations, unsupported novelty claims, confusing examples, and overconfident language about profit.

Review records must say what was actually read, what was checked, which issues were found, how they were resolved, and which limitations remain. A generated word count or source inventory is not evidence that an editor read those words or inspected those sources.

The manuscript inventory command uses standard-library Python from the trading repository root:

python book\scripts\manuscript_inventory.py

Its only purpose is to make coverage explicit and help readers locate the files. It does not score the quality of the writing or certify the statistical evidence.

The manuscript checks and companion checks are now separate. From the trading repository root:

python book\scripts\assemble_claims.py --check
python -m unittest discover -s book\tests -q

Run educational Python examples, code tests, and the NOAA study from book\companion, using that project's .venv; see the companion README. Historical review counts and commands describe the pre-relocation work and are not new validation claims for the directory move.

docs.title: Relocation note
docs.text: This is the completed pre-relocation editorial record, not a new full-manuscript review or a new test run. Historical findings, coverage, numerical results, and counts below are preserved. Paths in the coverage/file lists have been translated to the current layout: research and reviews are under book, manuscript tools/tests are under book\scripts and book\tests, and the educational Python project is under book\companion. The trading repository root is separate from that companion project. Current command equivalents appear below the historical validation record.

docs.title: Verdict and scope
docs.text:
Editorial corrections and parent integration are complete. The editor's handoff was conditional on rebuilding the aggregate claim map and completing release checks; the parent subsequently completed those actions, as recorded below. No additional blocking code defect was identified in this editorial alignment work.

This was an independent AI technical editorial pass by an agent that did not author the draft. It is not academic peer-review certification, a legal opinion, an originality/plagiarism certification, or evidence that a trading strategy is profitable. The actual manuscript was read, not merely its outline, inventory, or author summaries.

The handoff inventory reported 94,725 chapter prose words. At completion of this editorial pass, the manuscript word-count function reported 90,771, with the shortest chapter at 2,185 words. All 30 chapters remained substantive and exceeded the 1,600-word floor; the manuscript exceeded 60,000 words. The small excess over the soft 90,000-word target was not a release blocker. Reductions removed erroneous or repetitive explanations rather than trimming to a quota; worked derivations, exercises, and the final five practical guides remained. Later directory-navigation wording is not a new mathematical review or part of that historical word count.

No source-book text or repository was consulted. No commits, publication, dependency installation, source acquisition, funded orders, wallet operations, data refresh, or refreeze occurred. Source files, executable examples, manifests, tests, bibliography, frozen data/results, and the parent README were not edited.

docs.title: Substantive findings and resolutions
docs.text: Area Finding Resolution Chapters 1, 6, 20, 28 A fractional exceptional state was said necessarily to destroy complement pricing. Distinguished ordinary binary-label probabilities from full payoff vectors. A 0.50/0.50 pair still pays one unit in total. Added settlement-time, financing, collateral, and feasible-trading qualifications. Chapters 2-4 Odds direction was reversed; immediate taker execution was presented as all execution; Wolfers-Zitzewitz and Manski were assigned the same risk-neutrality premise. Corrected in-favor versus against odds, maker/taker distinctions, and the separate theoretical assumptions. Kept Berg's vote-share estimand and five-election limitation; removed any implied measured effective sample size. Chapter 5 Splitting an LMSR trade was said automatically to reduce its cost, contradicting path independence. A log identity was malformed. Derived telescoping split costs, repaired the stable log-sum-exp expression, required positive liquidity, and distinguished numerical safeguards from universal precision. Corrected fixed-point quantity strings and the loss-bound limiting argument. Chapter 6 and related claims USD 0.90 profit was called payout; a full-refund void appeared to be a documented general venue rule. Separated USD 5.00 receipts from USD 0.90 profit. Explicitly labeled refund conventions hypothetical and distinguished refunded fees from nonrefunded fees. Removed unsupported void attribution. Chapters 7-11 Different labels could be mistaken for independence; several passages required eventual labels at their own earlier forecast time. Distinguished dependence from contractual identity, feature decision cutoffs from fitting cutoffs, and legitimate future evaluation outcomes from leakage or target-vintage substitution. Corrected constructor, splitter, and evaluation-guard descriptions. Chapters 9-10 Fisher-transform uncertainty was described as raw correlation uncertainty, and dependence was said always to increase standard errors. Stated the transform and illustrative normal-theory assumptions; removed the universal variance-direction claim. Kept event and row counts separate. Chapter 10 The Brier uncertainty term was called an irreducible score floor; grouped forecasts were paired in the wrong order; the decomposition gap was attributed to the wrong term. Explained how resolution can offset uncertainty, corrected the grouped sequence, and derived the within-bin variance/covariance remainder. Distinguished sharpness from distance to a base rate. Chapters 10-12, 16, 19 Calibration fitting and evaluation cohorts were confused, and a worse toy score was presented as proof of a particular overfitting cause. Validation fits the map; test assesses it. Preserved the observed deterioration and qualified its possible explanation. Removed automatic-calibration recommendations. Chapters 11-12 Scaling, posterior inference, and boosting implementation were overstated. Explained scaling's penalty/conditioning role, posterior mode versus full posterior, and raw-gradient teaching updates versus the installed boosted classifier's initialization and leaf updates. Removed an unsupported learning-rate-times-stage score bound. Chapter 13 Minimum-variance linear averaging was said to require Gaussian unbounded variables and to leave the probability interval even with valid convex inputs. Derived the variance minimizer without that assumption and separated linear estimation from a Gaussian posterior model. Distinguished discrete hazard probabilities, continuous rates, event occurrence, and settlement delay. Chapters 14-15 Hand TF-IDF and sigmoid-network calculations were presented too close to literal descriptions of different installed defaults. Documented smoothed IDF, raw counts and L2 normalization; separated sigmoid hand derivations from the six-unit ReLU companion. Corrected feature-vector ordering and optimizer guarantees. Chapter 16 Minimum variance was equated with minimum Brier without a bias assumption; unconstrained weights were treated as probability weights; a blend could supposedly be worse than both components. Added zero-mean/second-moment conditions, convex constraints and degeneracy handling. Explained the convex-loss bound and separate weight-fitting/evaluation cohorts. Chapters 17, 20, 28 Ceiling notation omitted cent units; basket examples mislabeled flat-dollar fees as notional percentages. Defined cent ceiling, corrected fee units and checked both conventions. Aligned required_cash with the larger of modeled cost and summed reservations, without calling rounding a venue price tick. Chapter 20 Payoff-dominance trade direction and executable inequality were reversed. The nonnegative-payoff trade buys broad and sells narrow; strict cash-positive opportunity requires narrow bid above broad ask, under feasible shorting/creation assumptions. The companion remains long-only. Chapters 18, 24 Seven clocks were headed “six”; partial execution was confused with full-size screening failure; cancellation requests were conflated with effective cancellation. Corrected the count and distinct interfaces. Explicitly separated ordered paper replay from asynchronous venue match/cancel/receipt reconciliation. Chapter 21 Arrival intensities were equated to finite-window probabilities; expected loss and commitment limits were treated as maximum session-loss bounds. Recast the worked example as a coherent one-opportunity probability model, retaining its checked numbers. Distinguished payout risk, administrative settlement, outstanding commitments, and cumulative session loss. Chapter 22 Fee symbol f was reused for Kelly allocation; nonlinear costs were handled by plugging an average cost into a constant-cost optimum. Used phi in math notation, proved concavity, and derived the quantity-level log-wealth objective for nonlinear costs. Kept it explicitly unimplemented. Distinguished cash loss, payout notional, borrowing, and optional sizing objectives. Chapter 23 IPS missing finite-sample matches were described as undefined weights; timing and unbiasedness conditions were incomplete. Distinguished zero population propensity from an absent sampled match, documented the stricter code gate, and stated fixed-policy, logging, reward-consistency, and fitting-time conditions. Qualified weight ESS. Chapter 25 Correct equal-weight convex projection was said able to worsen aggregate squared error on a feasible realized outcome vector. Added the projection inequality and its narrow loss guarantee, while preserving empirical questions about calibration, incorrect edges, weights, coverage, execution, and genuine novelty. Chapters 26-30 A version lock was called hash-locked; fixed source code was treated as evidence of predeclaration; results were described as frozen before scoring. The proposed ask-only edit made a crossed book. Corrected environment and evidence claims, labeled output excerpts, and supplied a valid bid/ask sensitivity edit. Corrected basket error semantics, synthetic round-trip scope, and actual evidence-flag values. The manual-only closing boundary is unchanged. Claim fragments Several rows retained obsolete metadata-only descriptions, misclassified abstract inspection, or repeated corrected source/technical claims. Reconciled 14 rows in six fragment files with the existing audit's recorded depth and corrected manuscript. No source record was upgraded or new primary-text reading invented.

docs.title: Mathematical and numerical work
docs.text:
The canonical USD accounting remained unchanged: cost 4.10, binary profits 5.90 and minus 4.10, model-conditional EV 1.40, resale profit 0.40, and fractional-settlement profit 0.90 with no binary label.

Independent in-memory calculations checked:

  • LMSR ten-unit cost 6.201145 at liquidity 10, 5.124948 at liquidity 100, and equality of one ten-unit trade with successive four- and six-unit trades.
  • Raw/grouped Brier values 0.075/0.0625, zero perfect-forecast loss, and infinite wrong-certainty natural-log loss.
  • Logistic probability and both log-loss branches, the two-forecaster weight 0.272727 and variance 0.031818, and the three feasible outcome-vector projection comparisons.
  • The sigmoid hand network's forward pass and all nine parameter gradients, with central finite differences agreeing within 1e-8.
  • Fill-conditioned probabilities approximately 0.461078, 0.401993, and 0.328358, with ten-unit expected profits approximately 0.510778, minus 0.080066, and minus 0.816418.
  • Quarter-Kelly fraction 0.059322 under the stated constant-cost assumptions.
  • Flat-fee basket totals 10.10/9.90/9.82 versus notional-rate totals 9.96/9.86/9.82. The 0.3333-price regression case costs 2.02 but requires 2.10, rejecting the lower funding.
  • Chapter 27's original suggested ask-only modification raises crossed book is ambiguous; the corrected bid 0.14/ask 0.15 case returns a paper candidate with cost 1.60 and modeled profit 0.405420.
  • The normal-noise selection illustration: mean maxima about 1.867827 for 20 draws and 1.161329 for five; repeated-look false positives 24.8105% versus 5.032% at the single final look under the disclosed construction.

These checks are classroom derivation checks, not new empirical market experiments.

docs.title: Source and evidence limits retained
docs.text:
All 55 source records and their bibliography entries were compared with the manuscript's uses. This editor did not newly retrieve or independently reread the original papers. References to inspected sections describe the prior source audit's explicitly recorded work. The editorial pass checked consistency with that audit and independently verified the elementary arguments listed above; it does not certify every source theorem, proof, historical empirical analysis, or bibliographic identity anew.

BRIER1950, MURPHY1973, and FRIEDMAN2001 remain metadata-only pointers. Other entries retain their actual abstract-versus-section limits. Wolfers-Zitzewitz/Manski assumptions, Berg's vote-share target, Avellaneda-Stoikov's approximate finite-horizon simulation model, and White/Politis dependence limits remain qualified. Current documentation and a partial terms response do not establish permanent fees, legal eligibility, or unrestricted data rights.

The NOAA comparison is real current/final-vintage observational forecasting under a hypothetical clock, not market-price or profit evidence. The 17 default examples remain synthetic. Chapter 25 remains an untested research agenda, not proven novelty or alpha. No script gains a live-order path, persistent OMS, venue adapter, or automatic promotion mechanism.

docs.title: Technical review: companion and evidence infrastructure
Current locations of the reviewed materials
docs.text:
This is a historical record of the independent review before directory relocation, not a new code review or new test run. The reviewed educational Python project now lives in book\companion; its paper-only boundary does not describe separate trading-system code at the repository root. docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
A fresh, read-only code-review agent inspected the new Python companion diff independently of its implementer. The scope covered the paper ledger, contracts, costs, risk and basket decisions, probability models and evaluation, optional public-GET acquisition, offline examples, the NOAA study, and their relevant tests and environment files. The shared notation and example documentation served as behavioral contracts.

This was not the whole-manuscript editorial read. The separate editorial phase covers all chapters and their transitions. Neither review is academic peer review, a legal opinion, or certification of profitable trading.

docs.title: Findings and resolutions
docs.text:
Finding Resolution Evidence retained Paper screening reused original depth after the broker had consumed it. paper_decision now screens a read-only remaining-depth view. Screening, execution, and marking share the broker's consumption calculation. After ten units at 0.40 are consumed, a second twenty-unit screen uses the remaining 0.60 asks: cost 12.00 and modeled profit -1.00 at probability 0.55. Repeated screening leaves the original snapshot and ledger unchanged. Basket screening counted modeled fill cost but omitted conservative order reservations. The basket reports required_cash and checks enough funding to submit all legs before execution, using the same fee/reservation helper as the broker. Three units on each complementary leg at 0.3333 with an invented 0.001 unit fee cost 2.02 in aggregate fills but require 2.10 reserved cash. The lower capital is rejected; both orders can be submitted and filled with the higher capital. Evaluation blocked reused event IDs but allowed new event IDs from fitted dependence groups. Fitted forecasters retain both training and calibration group IDs, and evaluation rejects overlap with either. Regressions supply a distinct event in each fitted group type and require explicit rejection. Truncated chunked HTTP responses escaped the collector's structured failure path. HTTP protocol/read exceptions enter bounded retry handling and preserve completed-page and attempt diagnostics. A real in-memory HTTPResponse with a truncated chunk, retry exhaustion, a successful retry, response closure, and prior-page retention are exercised without network access.

The reviewer then inspected these focused fixes and their regressions, marked all four findings resolved, and reported no fix-introduced high-confidence issues. The reviewer independently ran the 136 companion and NOAA tests present at that point. Later manuscript-integrity checks are a separate activity rather than part of that historical count.

docs.title: Frozen-byte portability
docs.text:
Integration also exposed a persistence defect before the independent review: the frozen implementation and protocol included CRLF bytes, but the initially proposed LF checkout rules would have changed their hashes. Passing the study in the original worktree would not have proved reproduction after a fresh checkout.

The fix preserves the original hash-bound bytes with scoped Git -text rules. No source observations, protocol contents, shared scoring implementation, predictions, scores, or frozen evaluation were changed or selected again. A regression compares Git's filtered and unfiltered object hashes for every bound input and result file. Ordinary unbound package sources can still use their normal LF policy.

docs.title: Evidence and operating boundaries
docs.text:
The research ledger distinguishes inspected sections, inspected abstracts, metadata-only reading pointers, and official documentation. At source-audit completion it held 55 sources and a 73-row foundational claim map; authored chapter fragments extend that map. BRIER1950, MURPHY1973, and FRIEDMAN2001 retain disclosed access limitations rather than fabricated full-text verification.

All seventeen default demonstrations remain offline and explicitly synthetic. The optional acquisition interface preserves venue-native public snapshots, requires deliberate acknowledgement, and has no credential, signing, deposit, funded-order, or automatic promotion route. Its tests use synthetic HTTP responses; they do not establish current account eligibility or redistribution permission.

The real NOAA study remains a frozen current/final-vintage forecasting exercise with a hypothetical information clock, not historical prediction-market or executable-profit evidence. The paper ledger remains in-memory, single-process, and subject to its explicitly invented USD fee and quantity conventions. Supplied maker fills, complete payout-state declarations, and evidence flags are assumptions to audit, not mechanisms that turn uncertain inputs into facts.

docs.title: Review limitations
docs.text: The review and regressions reduce specific implementation risks; they do not prove the absence of all defects. They do not validate a real exchange's fills, queue dynamics, latency, fees, legal availability, or a strategy's future returns. The accompanying source ledger and data-provenance records retain their narrower, explicitly stated inspection and measurement limits.
